messages:
mira: quick status — ran the int4 -> int6 hybrid sweep on muon11b. latency down ~14% p50 vs int4, but QA F1 on long-form QA dropped ~2.8% on our conversational set. logs below.

sam: can you paste the benchmark snapshot? numbers plz

mira: sure — summary from local canary: ```
model variant | p50 latency | p95 latency | QA-F1 (conv set) | mem delta
int4         | 112ms       | 330ms      | 0.812            | baseline
hybrid-int6  | 96ms        | 290ms      | 0.789            | +4%
int8 (ref)   | 140ms       | 410ms      | 0.815            | +12%
```

mira: note: p50 measured at batch_size=8, max_new_tokens=256, on A100-80; mem delta is host-visible fragmentation estimate (heap delta).

oliver: 2.8% F1 regression is small but consistent across seeds? could be quantization bias on numerics or tokenization edgecases. did you run long prompts?

mira: yes — longest prompts (context ~2k tokens) show the worst regressions, esp Q->A with many code blocks. short QA <256 prompt shows negligible delta.

kai: interesting — could be kv-cache float->quant mixing when prefix is long. any OOMs?

mira: we saw some OOM spikes when batch_size>=12 with hybrid-int6, not with int4. memory fragmentation climbs after steady-state ~30min. stack trace points to slab allocations in the slot compactor. attached snippet: ```
[warn] evict: cannot shrink slab 0x7f... after 3 tries
[err] alloc: failed to reserve 4MB for new kv stripe
```

sam: so tradeoffs are latency vs QA + mem stability. is QA drop recoverable with prompt engineering / decoding tweaks?

mira: quick ablation: using greedy -> top-p 0.95 reduced the F1 gap to ~1.3%, beam search eliminated gap but tripled latency. So decoding interacts with quant error.

oliver: maybe lower default max_new_tokens for convo-style endpoints to reduce long-kv volatility. dynamic cap based on prompt_len seems sensible.
kai: agree. propose: rollout plan — 1) lock hybrid-int6 for short-prompts (prompt_len <= 512) with batch_size default 8, 2) keep int4 for long-context routes, 3) set dynamic max_new_tokens = min(256, max(64, prompt_len*0.5)).

mira: initial canary results with dynamic cap: p50 latency +1% vs hybrid default, QA-F1 restored to 0.806 (within 0.6% of int4). memory fragmentation drops ~2.5% in steady-state.

eng-ml-bot: perf test matrix run queued: job-id=muon-hybrid-8000001111-01, ETA 45m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: we should add a small-quality eval in the canary gating — for any quant variant where F1 drop >1% trigger fallback. also track regen rate for multi-turn.

mira: agreed. i'll add an eval with 500 convo prompts and a small hallucination heuristic.

devops-bot: alerted cluster-3 about the canary — pinned to A100-80 pool, capacity request 6 GPUs.

oliver: ops question — for the slab issue, can we pre-reserve an extra 16MB per instance for kv growth to reduce compactor churn?
kai: last time we pre-reserved we saw memory waste on low-load instances but improved stability. maybe do adaptive reserve: allocate + reserve only when steady-state mem churn > threshold.

mira: implementation notes: patch in runtime to expose kv_slab_reserve config and a runtime metric kv_slab_churn. will default to off, canary on for hybrid-int6. code snippet: ```json
{"kv_slab_reserve_mb":16, "kv_slab_churn_threshold_pct":8}```

sam: rollout checklist?

mira: 1) eng-ml-bot perf run (in flight)
2) deploy runtime patch to canary ring with kv_slab_reserve=16
3) gated canary for 4 hours observing F1 and kv_slab_churn
4) if F1 delta <=1% and no OOMs, expand to 20% of serving capacity
5) full rollout with autoscale policy tuned

kai: add an emergency fallback: if OOM rate crosses 0.5% over 10m, route traffic to int4 variant automatically.

mira: noted. I'll draft the PR and the canary run config. anyone want to take ownership for the runtime metric alert?

oliver: I can own metric + alert. will add dashboards: kv_slab_churn, per-variant QA-F1, regen-rate, p50/p95.

sam: thanks — once PR is up @mira ping eng-rl and we can re-run evaluation harness for safety.

mira: thanks all. will post PR link here when ready. :rocket:
